prompt_src:
Kindly summarize the text below in XML format. Make sure the summary contains less than 4 sentences.

Quantum entanglement is the phenomenon that occurs when a group of particles are generated, interact, or share spatial proximity in such a way that the quantum state of each particle of the group cannot be described independently of the state of the others, including when the particles are separated by a large distance. The topic of quantum entanglement is at the heart of the disparity between classical and quantum physics: entanglement is a primary feature of quantum mechanics not present in classical mechanics.

Measurements of physical properties such as position, momentum, spin, and polarization performed on entangled particles can, in some cases, be found to be perfectly correlated. For example, if a pair of entangled particles is generated such that their total spin is known to be zero, and one particle is found to have clockwise spin on a first axis, then the spin of the other particle, measured on the same axis, is found to be anticlockwise. However, this behavior gives rise to seemingly paradoxical effects: any measurement of a particle's properties results in an apparent and irreversible wave function collapse of that particle and changes the original quantum state. With entangled particles, such measurements affect the entangled system as a whole.

Such phenomena were the subject of a 1935 paper by Albert Einstein, Boris Podolsky, and Nathan Rosen, and several papers by Erwin Schrödinger shortly thereafter, describing what came to be known as the EPR paradox. Einstein and others considered such behavior impossible, as it violated the local realism view of causality (Einstein referring to it as "spooky action at a distance") and argued that the accepted formulation of quantum mechanics must therefore be incomplete.

Laburtu mesedez beheko testua XML formatuan. Ziurtatu laburpenak 4 esaldi baino gutxiago dituela.

Interangulazio kuantikoa partikula-talde bat sortu, elkarreragin edo gertutasun espaziala partekatzean gertatzen den fenomenoa da, halako moldez non taldeko partikula bakoitzaren egoera kuantikoa ezin baita deskribatu besteen egoeratik aparte, baita partikulak distantzia handi batez bananduta daudenean ere. Korapilatze kuantikoaren gaia fisika klasikoaren eta kuantikoaren arteko ezberdintasunaren muinean dago: korapiloa mekanika klasikoan ez dagoen mekanika kuantikoaren ezaugarri nagusia da.

Propietate fisikoen neurketak, hala nola, posizioa, momentua, biraketa eta polarizazioa partikula korapilatuetan, kasu batzuetan, erabat korrelatuak daudela egiazta daiteke. Adibidez, bi partikula korapilatu sortzen badira, haien biraketa osoa zero dela jakiten da, eta partikula batek erloju-orratzen biraketa duela lehen ardatz batean, orduan beste partikularen biraketa, ardatz berean neurtua, antizikloia dela aurkitzen da. Hala ere, jokabide honek itxuraz paradoxikoak diren ondorioak sortzen ditu: partikula baten propietateen neurketa orok partikula horren uhin funtzioaren kolapso itxurazko eta atzeraezina eragiten du eta jatorrizko egoera kuantikoa aldatzen du. Partikula korapilatuekin, neurri horiek sistema korapilatuari eragiten diote.

Horrelako fenomenoak izan ziren Albert Einstein, Boris Podolsky eta Nathan Rosenen 1935eko artikulu baten gaia, baita handik gutxira Erwin Schrödingerrek kalertutakoena, EPR paradoxa bezala ezagutzen zena deskribatuz. Einsteinek eta beste batzuek ezinezkotzat jotzen zuten jokabide hori, kausalitatearen tokiko errealismoaren ikuspuntua bortxatzen baitzuen (Einsteinek "urruneko ekintza mamitsua" bezala aipatzen zuen), eta mekanika kuantikoaren formulazio onartuak, beraz, osatugabea izan behar zuela defendatzen zuten.
